header.tag_why: The deal turned at the store ops workshop. When Bev asked who does the installs, our answer was a partner and we had nobody who had run a store rollout, while Adyen arrived with a retail team that had done store rollouts and offered one contract.

messaging_changes.current_line: Online and in-store on one platform; the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
messaging_changes.change: For store-led retail deals, where the head of store operations or the COO is in the room: replace this line with the buyer's own words, 'One system for the tills and the website,' and follow it immediately with a live, step-by-step walkthrough of an online order being returned at a store till. Only use the walkthrough after the solutions engineer confirms it can be shown live. Do not describe it.
messaging_changes.why: Bev dismissed our line with 'that's a diagram.' She then asked how a return works 'Step by step. At the till.' and kept repeating 'One system for the tills and the website,' and we described the return instead of showing it.

messaging_changes.change: For retailers with store rollouts: add a line and a proof point on single accountability, framed around the buyer's fear: 'I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.' Name who owns installs and store rollout end to end. If partners do the installs, state that we are the one accountable party. Back the line with a template rollout plan covering 'Dates, who installs, what happens to the old tills.' Bring someone who has run a store rollout to the store workshop.
messaging_changes.why: Our answer on installs was a partner, and nobody on our side had run a store rollout. Adyen offered rollout veterans and one contract, which speaks directly to the stated fear of two vendors pointing at each other.

messaging_changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
messaging_changes.change: For store-led retail deals: offer a peer retailer they can talk to, and line up a reference call that can be arranged quickly, instead of pointing to customer stories. Suggested line: 'Talk to a retailer who has rolled us out across their stores.'
messaging_changes.why: The buyer asked 'can I talk to them?' and we couldn't set up a call in time, while Adyen named retailers Angela knew.

messaging_changes.change: For retail pitches aimed at the COO and store operations: open with the store problem, not checkout conversion. Lead with 'Buy online, return in store' at the till and a loyalty program that works everywhere because it is 'one customer, one basket.' In retail copy, say 'the tills' rather than 'point of sale', 'in-person payments' or 'unified commerce'.
messaging_changes.why: The evaluation was triggered by store returns and split customer records. The customer described it as 'one customer, one basket' and 'the tills,' and never used our category terms.

trigger.insight: This evaluation started as a store operations problem: returns at the till and split customer records. It was never a web checkout problem. The origin story inside the company centers on the COO in a store, not the CTO, which pointed to who would own the decision long before the signature did.
trigger.messaging: Lead retail pitches with the cross-channel return and the single customer record (buy online, return at the till, loyalty that works everywhere), not with checkout conversion.

decider.insight: Angela signed with Adyen, and her team asked for the store workshop. Yet the rep first named Raj as the decider, because Raj ran the RFP and was his contact. We sold to the process owner and met the person who signed once, at the kickoff. Raj's support for us rests only on what he told the rep, and it is unclear how much weight his view carried.
decider.messaging: When the trigger is operational pain, aim retail messaging and proof at the COO and store operations as the economic buyer, not only at the CTO who runs the RFP.

competitor.insight: By Raj's account, Adyen pitched people, peers and accountability: rollout veterans, retailers Angela knew, and one contract. That is a direct answer to Angela's fear of two vendors pointing at each other. After they met Adyen, 11 of the customer's 14 questions were about stores, so the evaluation moved away from the web ground we were winning. Everything about Adyen's pitch reached us only through Raj, after the decision.
competitor.messaging: Counter 'one platform, one contract' with a named retail rollout team and peer retailer references, rather than restating the platform claim.

message.insight: M3 failed with exactly the audience it is meant for. Bev, the head of store operations, dismissed it as a diagram and immediately asked for the operational steps, which the rep could only describe. The part that landed, the checkout demo, impressed the ecommerce lead, who was not the person who signed.
message.messaging: Replace the M3 line in store-led deals with a step-by-step, live walkthrough of an online order returned at a till.

decided.insight: The rep felt the deal was lost at the workshop. The customer brought six store operations people; we brought an AE and a solutions engineer, and our answer on installs was a third party. To a COO who doesn't want two vendors pointing at each other, that partner answer may have recreated the exact problem, though why Bev stopped asking questions is not established. Being 'ahead' was Raj's view, and Raj was not the signer.
decided.messaging: State plainly who owns installs and store rollout end to end, and if partners are involved, position us as the single accountable party.

gaps.insight: The customer asked us for three proofs: a retailer to call, a rollout plan, and a live return at the till. We delivered none of them; we sent a case study and gave descriptions instead. M8's 'see our customer stories' is the wrong format for this buyer, because Angela wanted a conversation with a peer. It is unclear whether the live return demo was missing because of the product or because of preparation.
gaps.messaging: For store deals, back M8 with a reference call that can be arranged quickly and a live cross-channel return demo, plus a template rollout plan (dates, installer, old-till handling).

language.insight: The customer described outcomes and accountability: one system, one customer, one basket, no vendor finger-pointing. We described categories: unified commerce, in-person payments, point of sale. Bev repeated 'One system for the tills and the website' every time, and we never adopted it.
language.messaging: Use 'the tills', 'one customer, one basket' and single-vendor accountability in retail copy instead of 'unified commerce' and 'point of sale'.

gaps.question: What was the deal size (ACV)?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom what ACV was proposed, and whether Raj ever shared Adyen's commercial terms.

gaps.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom, and Raj if he is reachable, what role Raj's recommendation played in Angela's decision and whether Angela ever saw our final proposal.

gaps.question: What did they use before (incumbent)?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom which payment and till provider the customer used before the RFP.

gaps.question: Did the web business also go to Adyen, or only stores?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom whether any part of the business (for example online checkout) stayed open to us.

gaps.question: Why couldn't we show a live till return or arrange a reference call in time?
gaps.follow_up: Ask the solutions engineer whether a live online-to-till return demo exists, and ask Tom what blocked the reference call.

gaps.question: How did we answer the store questions (wifi drops, rollout, Saturday till outages)?
gaps.follow_up: Ask Tom for our written replies to Raj's 14 questions.

close.rep_takeaway: When the pain started in the stores, the store side holds the pen, whoever runs the RFP. Get in front of the signer more than once, bring people who have done store rollouts to a store workshop, and when a buyer asks to see something, show it live instead of describing it.
